doc: Per-method classification used by the website to render Detailed Results chips, including historical published rows. Each method carries (a) a heaviness level anchored on the Python baseline wall time at the published bench scale (~2 MiB text input, 3 iters, 1 worker per cf6e8e7), and (b) an optional lifecycle status (active/deprecated/retired/retired-media) with the version it changed in. Match is case-insensitive substring on the bench label; longest match wins. Retired methods are absent from default artifacts and current benchmark runs; their old measurements remain here only to explain published historical results.

low.label: Low
low.explanation: Under 100 ms in the cited Python benchmark configuration. Measure the intended input and host before setting an operational limit.

medium.label: Medium
medium.explanation: 100 ms to 1 s in the cited Python benchmark configuration. Runtime and memory use depend on the input, KDF policy, and host.

high.label: High
high.explanation: 1 s to 5 s, or hundreds of MiB peak RSS, in the cited Python benchmark configuration. Measure resource use for the intended workload.

extreme.label: Extreme
extreme.explanation: Over 5 s, or multi-GiB peak RSS, in the cited Python benchmark configuration. Measure resource use for the intended input and host.

deprecated.label: Deprecated
deprecated.explanation: Public API stays callable so existing blobs / call sites keep working, but the method is no longer recommended for new code. Emits a deprecation warning at compile time and (where applicable) at first call. See CHANGELOG for the alternative.

retired.label: Retired
retired.explanation: Retired from default artifacts and current benchmark runs. Existing blobs still decode through an explicitly built compatibility artifact; historical result rows retain the retirement story.

retired-media.label: Retired 3.8.0 · compatibility build
retired-media.explanation: Retired, and excluded from default artifacts. Default C++, Java, and Python builds do not compile or package this method, its CLI command, its functional tests, or its benchmark. Existing data still decodes, but only from a compatibility artifact built with BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1 at the same BaseFWX version; the switch cannot restore code that was never packaged.

methods.notes: SHA-512 with fixed-size output.
Retired in 3.8.0. This non-standard hash chain includes a SHA-1 compatibility hop and adds no security property. Existing callers need a compatibility build. Use hash512 or SHA3-512 for new code.
Standard Base64 encoding. Work scales with input size.
AES-256-GCM benchmarked with the test-only 32,768-iteration PBKDF2 override.
Retired in 3.8.0. Its custom SHA-256 prefilter adds no security property. Existing callers need a compatibility build. Use hash512 or SHA3-512 instead.

Retired lossless carrier packing for PNG or WAV output. It is absent from default artifacts and current benchmarks. Decode existing files with a compatibility build using BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1.
Retired decoder for kFMe carrier PNG and WAV files. Decode existing files with a compatibility build using BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1.

Streaming AEAD with runtime-configurable authenticated frames and optional ffmpeg piping. Python defaults to 64 KiB frames; C++ and Java default to 1 MiB. The cited Python 2 MiB run measured about 470 ms.
Retired PNG-only carrier encoder. It is absent from default artifacts and current benchmarks. Existing callers need a compatibility build using BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1.
Retired decoder for legacy kFAe PNG carriers. Decode existing files with a compatibility build using BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1.
Decodes AN7 numeric transport output.
AN7 combines chunked AES-CTR, sparse bit flips, and a super-block permutation. Compare runtimes only at the same input size and chunk configuration.
AES-256-GCM benchmarked with the suite's PBKDF2 policy. Check the report's recorded iteration count before comparing results.

Numeric encoding for channels that accept digits only. Each fixed-width block includes an FNV-1a checksum. The Python path performs the transform in an interpreter loop, so runtime differences are expected.

Retired in BaseFWX 3.7.0 and absent from default artifacts and current benchmarks. Existing blobs still decode through a compatibility build. Use base64 for reversible transport encoding or hash512 for a digest.

Retired in 3.8.0. This reversible obfuscation method depends on retired b256 and has no security goal. Existing callers need a compatibility build. Use Base64 for transport or authenticated encryption for secrecy.

Password-required authenticated text payload. Version 3 uses AES-256-GCM with distinct HKDF/AAD domains and canonical standard base64. The password KDF dominates runtime; historical token expansion adds no cryptographic strength.

Password-or-master-keyed authenticated text payload. Version 3 uses AES-256-GCM with distinct HKDF/AAD domains and canonical standard base64. The password KDF dominates runtime; historical token expansion adds no cryptographic strength.
Retired whole-buffer media cipher with an optional archive trailer for exact restore. Decode existing files with a compatibility build using BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1.
File-mode b512 wrapper with KDF work and whole-file authenticated encryption.
File-mode pb512 wrapper with KDF work and whole-file authenticated encryption.
